text:
aj: Heads up — during a small canary change this morning (cohort bump 1% -> 5%) we saw a short spike in quota evictions and backend backpressure. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/evict/xyz

maria: I saw that too. Eviction rate ~3x for ~90s after apply. Console logs show a tight cluster of config_apply events.

kevin: Did the console do a live apply or a staged/dry-run?

aj: It was an in-console live apply — click 'apply' from preview, UI said "apply in background". No dry-run was performed.

elena: Which routes were affected? can you paste the operator events?

aj: sample from control-plane logs:
```
2026-03-23T10:12:34Z INFO config_apply apply_id=ap-9932 target_cohort=5% affected_shards=[s1,s3,s7]
2026-03-23T10:12:34Z INFO propagate shard=s1 to=coord-12 status=queued
2026-03-23T10:12:35Z WARN eviction_trigger shard=s1 rate=120/s
2026-03-23T10:13:45Z INFO config_apply_complete apply_id=ap-9932 duration_ms=71000
```
Looks like propagation fan-out lined up and triggered short-lived hot reads on config store + eviction work.

sam: That matches an existing pattern — our current propagation broadcasts to all coordinators in parallel which can spike work on certain shards when many coordinators re-evaluate quotas simultaneously.

priya: We made parallel apply the default to minimize activation latency, but this shows an operational cost. We should offer a "safe apply" mode that staggers propagation.

kevin: Proposal: extend config-apply API with optional fields: `stagger_window_ms` and `max_concurrent_shards`. Defaults keep current behavior but console can use safe defaults. Also add `apply_mode:\"fast|safe\"`.

maria: Telemetry-wise we should run a preflight simulation for big cohort jumps (>2%) that estimates expected evictions and peak latency. Console should show the estimate and require a confirmation if risk > threshold.

ops-bot: incident created: #inc-2026-231 assigned to @oncall-platform — auto-notify oncall.

elena: Additionally, add a server-side rollback-on-surge guard: if eviction_rate > X for Y seconds revert apply_id. That would reduce blast radius for accidental large changes.

aj: UX request — console should warn when a change >2% is applied within 1h of previous change, and surface an "apply rate" slider (seconds/minutes) so PMs can choose speed.

sam: Implementation note: the apply path needs idempotent apply tokens and a progress stream. We have apply_id now but not a real-time progress/probe API. We should emit progress events per shard apply with backoff hints.

priya: I can prototype the API with shape: `apply_id`, `stagger_window_ms`, `max_parallel_shards`, `allowed_burst_tokens`. Will open a RFC + PR linking console UX.

maria: Add a telemetry contract: emit `preflight_estimate` (evictions_est, latency_p95_delta_est) and `actual_apply_summary` (evictions_count, peak_latency_delta, reverted=true/false). That will let us validate preflight accuracy.

kevin: Agree. Also update the runbook to call out: when apply causes eviction spike, run `config rollback apply_id` and check `eviction_rate` and `quota_health` dashboards. Console should surface a one-click rollback if the guard trips.

aj: Can we get a PoC for the staggered apply + console warning by EOD? If not, we should temporarily change console to require manual small step applies for cohort jumps >2%.

priya: I'll start the PR today and add unit tests for parallelism limits.

elena: I'll draft the telemetry schema and runbook updates.

maria: I'll add the preflight simulation hook to the telemetry backlog and mock up the console confirm copy.

aj: Thanks all — this feels like a good set of safety levers (stagger, preflight, auto-rollback, console UX). Ping here when PRs are up and we'll schedule a quick ops drill.
